# sevra — the command line for the Sevra hub

> The Sevra hub (https://www.sevrahq.com) is the managed home for db.md
> brains: databases in plain files, operated by the customer's own AI. sevra
> is the hub's product CLI — a signed, self-updating static binary. It is a
> machine interface: agents are its primary users.

Install (no runtime, no package manager). macOS/Linux, x86_64/arm64:

    curl -fsSL https://www.sevrahq.com/install/sevra.sh | sh

Windows (native x64, first release after v0.1.4; ARM64 via built-in emulation):

    irm https://www.sevrahq.com/install/sevra.ps1 | iex

Authenticate — approve once in the browser, no key to paste:

    sevra login
    # opens your person's browser; they approve; you get a session.
    # Headless/SSH: it prints a short code + URL to approve from any device.
    # Scripts/CI: sevra login --key sevra_account_... (minted in the dashboard).

Agent contract:
- Add `--json` to ANY command: machine-readable JSON on stdout, always,
  including errors ({"error": ...}); exit code 1 on failure, 2 on usage
  errors (bad flags/arguments), 0 with {"help"/"version"} for --help/--version.
- Notices go to stderr, never stdout.
- Config: ~/.sevra/config.json (0600). Env SEVRA_HUB_URL / SEVRA_API_KEY
  override it. Non-HTTPS hubs are refused (localhost exempt).

Commands:
    login [--hub <url>] [--no-browser] [--key <k>] | logout | whoami
    brains | create <slug> [--name --scope --public]
    delete <brain> [--confirm <slug>]     # PERMANENT, owner-only. Non-TTY/scripted runs
                                          # must pass --confirm with the brain's exact slug;
                                          # interactive runs are prompted for it.
    clone <brain> [dir]                   # first sync on a machine: verified records +
                                          # declared assets into a fresh directory, plus
                                          # .sevra-sync.json (brain/feed/pack/path baseline)
    pull [dir] [--force]                  # refresh that clone. Refuses and names local
                                          # divergence before network access; --force is
                                          # the explicit discard-local-work path. Hard-killed
                                          # commits recover before the next network request.
    push <dir> --brain <id|slug> [--force] [--allow-secrets]
                                          # REPLACES the hosted store with <dir> (files absent
                                          # locally are removed); --force allows a shrinking
                                          # replacement. Preflights the hub limits locally
                                          # (256 MiB pack / 512 MiB raw / 100k files, largest
                                          # files listed) and refuses secret-shaped markdown,
                                          # asset bytes, or names unless --allow-secrets.
                                          # Asset inspection is SHA-bound UTF-8, capped at
                                          # 8 MiB each / 64 MiB total, and reports omissions.
                                          # A `.sevralocal`
                                          # at the store root (one path/glob per line, `#`
                                          # comments) keeps matching files HOME: part of the
                                          # brain, never part of the cargo; the list never
                                          # uploads either, and while it has entries derived
                                          # index.md catalogs stay home too. DB.md and
                                          # assets.jsonl must always ride (a list covering
                                          # them is refused). Successful push records the
                                          # local baseline; later pushes are refused if the
                                          # durable hub feed advanced. --force explicitly
                                          # replaces that newer state.
    query <brain|--brain <ref>> [text] [--type --layer --meta-type --tag --where k=v --limit N]
    get <brain> <id|path> | graph <brain> <path> [--dir in|out|both]
    mcp                                   # stdio MCP server over the read surface
                                          # (list_brains, search_brain, get_record,
                                          # graph); client config
                                          # {"command":"sevra","args":["mcp"]}
    grant <brain> <email> [--write] | grants <brain> | revoke <brain> <grantId>
    shared | publish <brain> | unpublish <brain>
    secrets list|set|delete <brain> [NAME]
                                          # the vault (write-only values for published
                                          # functions). set reads the VALUE from stdin —
                                          # pipe it: printf %s "$V" | sevra secrets set b NAME
                                          # (one trailing newline trimmed); NEVER argv,
                                          # never echoed. NAME: ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$
    secrets scan [dir]                    # push's secret scan, read-only, offline: exit 1 on
                                          # matches ({"secretHits":[{path,kind,inPath}],
                                          # "total", "assetSecretScan", "error"}), 0 clean;
                                          # values never shown; honors .sevralocal
                                          # (kept-home files never ride)
    secrets quarantine [dir] [--dry-run] [--closure]
                                          # keep hit files home: scans the FULL store and
                                          # appends each hit file's exact path to .sevralocal
                                          # (created if absent; idempotent). Forward-only:
                                          # retained packs keep what already rode; declared
                                          # kept assets are not swept; backups retain ~31d.
                                          # Rotate first; erasure requires brain delete + the
                                          # retention window + fresh push. --closure also marks
                                          # wiki-linked files (needs dbmd). Never marks DB.md
                                          # or assets.jsonl (they ride; edit those). --json:
                                          # {marked, closureMarked, alreadyCovered, warnings,
                                          # total, note}
    inbox list|drain <brain>              # drain prints full JSON (BYO-agent read half)
    export <brain> [dir]                  # your brain back on disk
    validate [dir]                        # shells `dbmd validate --all`
    version | update                      # signed self-update; reports stale dbmd

Updates: the binary checks /api/hub/versions at most once a day and
self-updates only after both Ed25519 verification (pinned key) and the
independently deployed Sevra digest pass. SEVRA_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 disables.

Related: db.md, the open standard the hub hosts — https://github.com/carloslfu/db.md
(its CLI `dbmd` is the neutral format tool; sevra wraps it, never reimplements it).
